title: Throughput sprint snapshot — kernel/KV/batching (Oct 20 2026)
content:
Overview:

This note summarizes the serving-runtime work this sprint focused on throughput improvements across the kernel layer, KV cache behavior, and batching heuristics. The intent is to capture measured results from the two experiments we ran, outstanding risks for the upcoming rollout, and concrete action items for next week. This is a working doc — rough notes from standups, bench runs, and the post-mortem discussion on Oct 21.

Key progress this week:
- Kernel: final internal prototype of the fused-attention kernel (patch set in PR 1873) landed on the feature branch. Microbenchmarks show ~12–18% GPU token/sec improvement on A100-80GB for seq_len=1024. The fused kernel reduces kernel launch overhead and improves L2 reuse for attention keys.
- KV cache: implemented tiered eviction prototype (hot/near-cold split) and a cache-admission heuristic based on request prefix frequency. Early staging results show 6% reduction in repeated token decoding for multi-turn chat workloads.
- Batching heuristics: added a dynamic window controller that expands the batching window by up to 8ms under low p95 pressure and shrinks it when p95 > SLO. This reduced RPCs per token by ~7% in throughput tests.

Experimental runs and metrics (summary):
- Bench harness: run name "wiki-threads-10k-seqlen-1024" (synthetic conversational trace derived from internal logs).
- Baseline (prod branch): 52.3k tokens/sec per A100 (p50=14ms, p95=96ms).
- Kernel-fused (feature branch): 59.1k tokens/sec per A100 (p50=12.2ms, p95=104ms). Note: p95 increased slightly in tail; likely due to co-scheduling interference in the test instance.
- KV-tiered + admission: with baseline kernel gave 55.6k tokens/sec and reduced token duplication by 6.1%. p95 unchanged.
- Combined (fused kernel + KV-tier + dynamic window): 64.0k tokens/sec (p50=11.8ms, p95=110ms). CPU-side overhead rose by ~3% in the runtime scheduler loop.

Interpretation:
- The fused kernel materially increases steady-state throughput, but we observed a small tail latency regression when combined with current co-scheduling settings. We suspect GPU context switches from background maintenance tasks (GC/metrics flush) amplify the tail.
- KV-tiered admission reduces redundant decoding but can increase scheduler complexity; we measured modest scheduler CPU overhead. It looks promising for customer patterns with long multi-turn sessions.
- Dynamic batching window improves overall unit economics (fewer RPCs) but needs tighter integration with our latency SLO controller to avoid tail regressions under sudden load spikes.

Blockers & risks:
1) Tail latency regression risk in combined config. Action: isolate maintenance jitter by pinning maintenance threads to separate cores in the perf cluster (assigned to Leo).
2) Memory pressure with KV-tiered policy at high concurrency. Action: add a soft cap that kicks into a stricter eviction policy; run stress harness with up to 32 concurrent sessions (assigned to Maya).
3) Compatibility of fused kernel with quantized model paths (int8/4-bit). Action: compatibility tests on quantized runner and a fallback path if kernel unsupported (assigned to Ava).
4) Canary rollout dependencies: rollout requires a new autoscaler tweak and a canary guardrail in rollout service to prevent >10% capacity consumption by canary (work with platform-engineering).

Decisions made this week:
- Short-term: Ship fused kernel behind feature flag with default off for Dedicated customers. Enable for hosted API in a canary region for US-west-2 only.
- Medium-term: Merge KV-tiered admission into beta branch, but gate aggressive eviction with a runtime flag exposed in Dedicated config.
- Rollouts: require two consecutive 24-hour canaries with telemetry showing no >5% p95 regression and no >3% error-rate increase.

Action items (owners & timeline):
- Rohan: prepare the canary plan doc (includes telemetry checks, rollback triggers) by 2026-10-24 and link to the rollout ticket (JIRA-RT-4321).
- Ava: run quantized compatibility matrices and open issues for any unsupported op kernels by 2026-10-23.
- Maya: run mem-pressure stress runs (32 concurrent multi-turn sessions) and report out on leak or eviction thrash by 2026-10-25.
- Leo: implement maintenance-thread isolation on perf cluster and re-run tail-latency bench by 2026-10-24.
- Platform-eng liaison (Priya S.): update canary guardrails in deployment service; target merge by 2026-10-26.

Notes from standups (short bullets):
- "Observed a weird 3x spike in scheduler syscall time at minute 17 of the perf run" — investigating with perf traces (Rohan).
- "We should consider a lightweight token-prefetch for hot prefixes to reap more wins from KV cache" — spike idea from Maya; prototyping in scratch branch.
- "If fused kernel increases L2 reuse, it might behave differently on H100; schedule test on H100 dev nodes" — scheduling (Leo).

Follow-ups & docs to update:
- Update the serving-runtime perf playbook with the new canary telemetry checks and rollback instructions (doc owner: Rohan).
- Add a short FAQ in internal docs about the feature flag and expected regressions for early canary customers.
- Link PR 1873 in the patch notes and document the recommended kernel flag for Dedicated config.

Meeting attendees (Oct 20 standup + Oct 21 deep-dive):
- Rohan Patel (owner), Ava Thompson, Maya Chen, Leo García, Priya Sharma (platform-engineering), Samir Okoye (SRE), Lucy Park (observability).

Open questions (to resolve before production rollout):
- What is an acceptable p95 delta for customers with tight latency SLOs? (product to confirm; Rohan -> product-hosted-api).
- Do we need a separate autoscaler profile for canaries running fused kernel workloads? (platform eng).

Appendix (quick commands & perf hints used during tests):
- Perf harness: ./tools/bench/run_perf --profile=wiki-threads-10k --seq=1024 --instances=4 --gpu-type=A100 --quant=fp16
- Scheduler debug flags enabled: SCHED_DEBUG=1 SCHED_WINDOW_MS=6
- PRs mentioned: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1873 (fused-attn), https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1866 (kv-tiered)
